title: Choose the page composition
question: Which composition should carry forward, and what feels false to the world? Approve one layout for the build; the navy, off-white, gold palette, logo, content, and wayfinding system stay fixed.

options.label: Split hero with route diagram
options.lineage: Civic wayfinding signs and service directories
options.thesis: A clear citizen question leads directly into three labeled service routes.
options.viewport: The citizen question and primary action share the left half; a branch diagram of SMS review, report, and public alerts occupies the right. Government and local-demo details sit below.
options.risk: The map-like branch can feel abstract unless the route labels remain dominant.

options.label: Full-width service directory
options.lineage: Civic wayfinding signs and service directories
options.thesis: The citizen question is followed by one broad, unmistakable route system.
options.viewport: A full-width heading band leads into a single route line branching to three wide, readable destination plaques. SMS review is primary; government access and the demo note follow below.
options.risk: Three destination plaques occupy more width; small screens must stack them without losing the route relationship.

options.label: Vertical service rail
options.lineage: Civic wayfinding signs and service directories
options.thesis: A persistent left rail keeps the citizen’s routes visible beside the task.
options.viewport: A navy side rail holds the supplied shield and routes; the off-white main field holds the citizen question and three stacked action plaques.
options.risk: A persistent desktop rail may consume too much room on narrow screens and needs a compact mobile form.
